header: The Govt: ofKhyber Pakhtunkhwa through Inspector General
body: For petitioner(s): Mr. Mehboob Ali Khan, advocate.

1. By this constitutional petition under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, the petitioner, Umar Fayyaz Khan, impugns order dated 20.05.2026 passed by the leamed Additional Sessions Judge-IV/ Ex-Officio Justice of Peace, Lakki Marwat. That order dismissed his Petition No.194/4 of 2026 under Section 22-A Cr.P.C, in which he sought a direction to the SHO, Police Station Dadiwala, to register a criminal case against Mst. Robina Bibi, her father Rabban Shah, Muhammad Bilal and Maulana Muhammad Younas.

2, The petitioner's case is that Mst. Robina Bibi is his lawfully wedded wife. She obtained an ex-parte decree dated 20.02.2025 for dissolution of marriage from the learned Judge Family Court, Lakki Marwat. He assailed the decree before this Court in W.P. No.17-Bl2026, and its operation was suspended vide order dated 15.01.2026. While the suspension was in force, and while he was away at Karachi eaming his livelihood, her father caused her Nikah to be solemnized with Muhammad .l Bilal through Maulana Muhammad Younas. Her father then lodged FIR No.76 dated 22.02.2026 against the petitioner at Police Station Dadiwala under Sections 506/ 34 PPC read with Sections 314 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Elimination of Custom of Ghag Act,2013. The petitioner's pre-arrest bail in that case was confirmed ot 27.04.2026. When the police did not entertain his own application for registration of a case, he approached the learned Justice ofPeace.

3. The leamed Justice of Peace called for comments from the SHO concemed, which described the petition as a counter-blast to the aforesaid FIR. On consideration of the record, he held that the petition had been instituted as a counter-blast to the criminal proceedings pending against the petitioner, and that the suspension order was not absolute but operated for a limited period. He further held that the facts, if proved, constituted an offence under Section 494PPC, which is non-cognizable and for which no direction for regishation of an FIR could be issued, and that the marital status of the parties, being sub iudice, would be determined in due course' He accordingly dismissed the petition for want of sufficient material to justifr invoking provision of Section 22-ACt.P.C.

4. Leamed counsel for the petitioner contends that the learned Justice of peace failed to appreciate the effect of the suspension order dated 15.01.2026. On his case, the marriage between the petitioner and Mst' Robina Bibi was subsisting when the subsequent Nikah was performed, so the private respondents committed cognizable offences and the police were bound to register an FIR under Section 154 Cr.P.C. We have heard learned counselatlengthandgonethroughtherecordwithhisableassistance. ( 5. The question for determination is whether the leamed Justice of Peace committed any illegality or jurisdictional error in declining to direct registration of an FIR. Answering it requires examining, in sequence, the nature and scope of the jurisdiction under Section 22-ACr.P.C, the effect of the interim order relied upon by the petitioner, the legal character of the offences alleged, and the circumstances in which the petition was brought.

6. The scope of the jurisdiction of an Ex-Officio Justice of Peace under Section 22-A(6), Cr.P.C. is no longer res integra. In Muhammad Bashir v. Stafion House OIIicer, Okara Cantt. and others @LD 2007 SC 539), the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that where the information received by the police discloses the commission of a cognizable offence, the police are under a statutory obligation to register the case, and the question of the truth or veracity of the allegations is not to be determined at that stage. Subsequently, in Younas Abbas and others v. Additional Sessions Judge, Chakwal and others (PLD 20f6 SC 5Ef), a larger Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the functions of an Ex-Officio Justice ofPeace under Section 22-A(6), Cr.P.C. are quasi-judicial in nature and are neither executive, administrative nor ministerial. While exercising such jurisdiction, he is required to examine the application and the available record and to exercise judicial discretion after due application of mind. The court further held that these functions are complementary to those of the police and do no! by themselves, amount to interference in the investigative domain of the police' The parameters goveming the exercise of constitutional jurisdiction by the High courts are equally applicable to an Ex-Officio Justice of Peace. In his separate note, His lordship Mr. Justice Manzoor Ahmad Malik, J. emphasised that such powers should not be ( unbridled or open-ended and identified safeguards against their misuse. Accordingly, the jurisdiction under Section 22-A(6), Cr.P.C. is to be exercised within the limits prescribed by law; it neither authorizes an inquiry into the truth or falsity of allegations nor permits the registration of a criminal case in disregard of the statutory classification and procedure applicable to the alleged offence.

7. The petitioner's whole case rests on the interim order dated 15.01.2026, which no longer holds the field. W.P. No.l7-B/2026 was dismissed by this Court vide judgment dated 18.06.2026. The Hon'ble Supreme Court then dismissed CPLA No.2785 of 2026 and refused leave vide order dated 21.10.2026. It is seffled law that an interim order is ancillary to the main /rs and merges in the final order. Once the main petition is dismissed, the interim order stands vacated as if it had never been passed, and no litigant can derive a lasting advantage from the mere pendency of proceedings. The decree dated 20.02.2025 has therefore attained finality and operates from the date of its passing. The leamed Justice of Peace rightly observed that the stay was not absolute. The plea that the marriage was subsisting at the time of the subsequent Nikah is, at the very least, seriously disputed and cannot fumish a basis for directing registration of an FIR.

t /y W 8. Even if the petitioner's version is accepted at face value, the allegation of a second marriage during the lifetime of a spouse athacts, if at all, Section 494 PPC. Section 495 PPC is attracted only where concealment of the former marriage is also alleged. Both offences are non-cognizable under the Second Schedule to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898' Section 496-8 PPC, which the petitioner has also invoked, deals with fomication. Its ingredients are distinct and cannot be inferred from the mere solemnization of a Niknh, which is the very antithesis of that offence. Moreover, Section 203-C Cr.P.C. mandates that no Cou( shall take cognizance of an offence under Section 496-8 PPC except on a complaint lodged before a Court of competent jurisdiction, which excludes registration of an FIR altogether. For a non-cogtizable offence, the officer in charge of a police station must proceed under Section 155 Cr.P.C. He is to enter the substance ofthe information in the prescribed register and refer the informant to the Magistrate, and he cannot investigate the case without an order of a competent Magistrate. What the law does not permit directly cannot be achieved indirectly through Section 22-ACI.P.C. The petitioner's remedy lies in a private complaint under Sections 190 and 200 Cr.P.C, or an application under Section 155(2) Cr.P.C, before the competent Magistrate.

9. It is also evident from the record that the petitioner approached the leamed Justice of Peace only after FIR No.76 had been lodged against him at the instance ofRabban Shah and his pre-arrest bail had been confirmed. The parties are locked in prohacted matrimonial and criminal litigation. In these circumstances, the learned Justice of Peace was justified in holding that the petition was a counter-blast. Where an altemate and efficacious statutory remedy is available and the controversy turns on disputed questions of fact, a direction for registration of a criminal case is not warranted. In lkram Ullah Khan Yousafzai, Excise und Taxation Officer, Peshawar and others v. Dr. Rizwan Ullah and otherc (2022 SCMR 576)' the Hon'ble Supreme Court set aside a direction for registration of a criminal case and left the aggrieved party to the remedy of a private complaint. ln Mst. Mudiha Bano v. Senior Superintendent of Police, / Complaint Cell South Karachi and others (2025 SCMR 1435), it declined to interfere with concurrent refusal to order registration of an FIR because other avenues of redress remained open. In Rai Ashraf and olhers v. Muhammad Saleem Bhatti and others (PLD 2010 SC 691), the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that constitutional jurisdiction under Article 199 is discretionary, requires cogent reasons, and does not extend to disputed questions of fact. The availability of an alternate remedy, including a private complaint, is also a relevant consideration against constitutional interference. These principles apply to the present case.
10. For the foregoing reasons, this petition, being devoid of merit, is dismissed in limine.
